data.jobspec:
#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH --job-name=NextflowQAPipeline
#SBATCH --workdir=.
#SBATCH --error=err/Nextflow-%j.err
#SBATCH --output=out/Nextflow-%j.out
#SBATCH --cpus-per-task=48

# --- BEGIN USER COMMANDS ---
module load java/8u131
module load intel/2017.1
module load R/3.6.1

module load singularity

CONTAINER=/gpfs/projects/bsc83/utils/containers/singularity/rdeanalysis.simg


srun singularity exec ${CONTAINER} Rscript /gpfs/projects/bsc83/Projects/Ebola/code/ebola/nextflow_pipelines/scripts/SC/05_DE_mast.R "/gpfs/projects/bsc83/Data/Ebola/02_scRNA-Seq_PBMCs/01_scRNA-Seq_inVivo_rhemac10/05_RObjects/03_prep/03_immune.combined.ready.rds" "/gpfs/projects/bsc83/Data/Ebola/02_scRNA-Seq_PBMCs/01_scRNA-Seq_inVivo_rhemac10/05_RObjects/04_DE/"
# --- END USER COMMANDS ---

reasons: Missing memory request: The job does not specify a memory requirement (e.g., --mem=<size> or --mem-per-cpu=<size>). This can lead to job failure due to out-of-memory errors or inefficient scheduling.
Missing time limit: The job does not specify a wall time limit (e.g., --time=<dd-hh:mm:ss>). The job will be subject to the partition's default limit and may be terminated prematurely.

Missing partition/queue specification: The job does not specify a target partition (e.g., --partition=<name>). It will be sent to the default partition, which may not be suitable for the requested resources.
issues: The script assumes the directories 'err' and 'out' exist in the working directory. The job may fail if they are not present before submission. Consider adding 'mkdir -p err out' to the script.

The R script is executed as a single task but requests 48 CPUs. It should be verified that the script is multi-threaded and can efficiently utilize all requested cores, otherwise resources will be wasted.
All file paths are hardcoded, which reduces the script's portability and reusability. Using environment variables or command-line arguments for paths is a better practice.
